highlights.content: [Skip to Main Content](#aws-page-content-main) AWS Blogs * [Home](/blogs/) * Blogs * Editions ## [Artificial Intelligence](/blogs/machine-learning/) # The attendee’s guide to the AWS re:Invent 2026 AI/ML track From November 30th to December 4th, Amazon Web Services (AWS) will hold its annual premier learning event: [re:Invent](/events/reinvent/). At this event, attendees will become stronger and more proficient in various areas of AWS technology through a variety of experiences: keynotes given by AWS leaders, interactive working sessions led by AWS experts, and [fun, immersive activities such as live entertainment and games at re:Play](/events/reinvent/experiences/uniquely-reinvent/). There are over [2,000 learning sessions](https://registration.awsevents.com/flow/awsevents/reinvent2026/eventcatalog/page/eventcatalog?search=) that focus on specific topics at various skill levels, and the AI/ML (AIM) track has more than [140 unique sessions](https://registration.awsevents.com/flow/awsevents/reinvent2026/eventcatalog/page/eventcatalog?search=AIM) for you to choose from. We’re here to help you identify the sessions that best fit your needs. Even if you can’t join in person, you can catch up with many of the sessions on demand and even watch the keynotes live. ## The basics: Session types If you can join us, then remember that we offer several types of sessions that can help maximize your learning in a variety of AWS topics. re:Invent attendees can choose to attend breakouts, chalk talks, builder sessions, workshops, and code talks. The breakout sessions are recorded and uploaded a few days after to the [AWS Events YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@AWSEventsChannel), while the rest are live non-recorded interactive sessions. Here are the details for each session type: * **Breakout sessions:** Attendees are in a lecture-style 60-minute informative session presented by AWS experts, customers, and partners. * **Chalk-talk sessions:** Attendees interact with presenters, asking questions, and using a whiteboard in session. * **Builder sessions:** Attendees participate in a one-hour session and build something. * **Workshop sessions:** Attendees join a two-hour interactive session where you work in a small team to solve a real problem using AWS services. * **Code talk sessions:** Attendees participate in engaging code-focused sessions where an expert leads a live coding session. * **Lightning talk sessions:** Attendees watch a 20-minute demo dedicated to either a specific service or customer story (located in the Venetian Expo Hall or Wynn/Encore Upper Convention Promenade). With so many sessions to pick from, it helps to know how the pieces fit together. Here is how AWS thinks about its AI offerings, so you can decide where to begin and where to focus. ## The AWS AI stack overview and tie-in to re:Invent sessions AWS offers a comprehensive AI portfolio in the cloud. It covers everything from the physical infrastructure and AI chips that power AI workloads up through ready-to-use agentic solutions that teams can adopt today. Understanding how these services work together helps you navigate re:Invent and focus on the sessions most relevant to what you’re building. highlights.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Best Local LLM for Coding: $0 Weights vs $2 API [2026] ![Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/tvance.webp) [Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/author/tvance/) Updated Nov 12, 2026 · 26 min read The best local LLM for coding in mid-November 2026 depends less on a leaderboard score than on three constraints: how much memory your machine has, what license the weights carry, and whether you can verify the files you download. Google’s [Gemma 4 family, released under Apache 2.0 with commercial use allowed](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemma-4/), OpenAI’s gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b, and Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3.1 Pro all compete for the same developer attention, yet they sit at very different points on the hardware ladder. Choosing among them is harder than the headlines suggest. Parameter counts run from small on-device variants to a model that Moonshot describes at the 3-trillion level, and “open” means something different in each license file. Readers who want the licensing side in isolation can start with our [open-weight license comparison](https://shattered.io/open-weight-models-license-comparison-6-families-16gb-2026/). The narrower question is which of these models should actually sit behind your editor, terminal agent or CI job. The short answer, with the evidence below. For a single developer with a 16 GB-class machine, gpt-oss-20b is the safest starting point because OpenAI ships it under Apache 2.0 and documents a small memory footprint. For a team with an 80 GB-class workstation, gpt-oss-120b is the next step up. Gemma 4 is the pick when you want the cleanest license and a size for every machine. Kimi K3.1 Pro is a server-class model, not a laptop model. DeepSeek, Qwen and Llama stay on the watch list because the evidence we could verify today does not support ranking them for local use. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Run a Coding Model on Your Own Hardware in November 2026 Three reasons keep pulling developers toward local inference: code privacy, cost predictability and independence from someone else’s deprecation calendar. The third reason got a live demonstration this week. On November 10, 2026, DigitalOcean published a release note that [pulled several open models from its serverless inference product](https://docs.digitalocean.com/notes/2026/inference-deprecate-oss-models-nov-2026/). The notice names Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct, and a research summary of the same notice reports that Gemma 4, Qwen 3.5 397B A17B and DeepSeek V4 Flash left serverless inference too, with DigitalOcean pointing users toward DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Gemma 4 stayed available on dedicated inference. Nothing was discontinued by its maker. A hosting decision simply removed a cheap endpoint, and every team that had wired a pipeline to it had to migrate. Weights on your own disk do not get deprecated that way. If you pin a model file and a runtime version, the behavior of your coding assistant stays the same next month, which matters when your test suite or your review bot depends on consistent output. That stability is the strongest practical argument for local, stronger than raw price. ### What the industry data says about open models Adoption data points the same direction, though unevenly. IDC’s 2025 FutureScape predictions for Asia-Pacific (excluding Japan) state: “By 2026, 60% of Asia-Pacific organizations are predicted to build applications using open-source AI foundation models.” The source is IDC’s developer and DevOps predictions document, and the figure is a forecast, not a measured result. highlights.content: [![Indian Television Dot Com](https://indiantelevision.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ITV-Logo-2.png)](https://indiantelevision.com/) Connect with us ### [Brands](https://indiantelevision.com/category/mam/marketing/brands/) # Global AI software revenue set to cross $200 billion in 2026 Omdia forecasts 30 per cent annual growth through 2031 as generative and agentic AI accelerate ![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/fd75cd9100da953cd4c7bf3ea9515c92d8799495b1f2ce564f477853da209df1?s=46&d=mm&r=g) Published 2 hours ago on By [indiantelevision.com Team](https://indiantelevision.com/author/indiantelevision-com-team/) [![Follow on Google News](https://indiantelevision.com/wp-content/themes/zox-news/images/google-news-logo.png)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqMQgKIitDQklTR2dnTWFoWUtGR2x1WkdsaGJuUmxiR1YyYVhOcGIyNHVZMjl0S0FBUAE) ![](https://indiantelevision.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/AI-2.jpg) [* Follow us on Google News](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqMQgKIitDQklTR2dnTWFoWUtGR2x1WkdsaGJuUmxiR1YyYVhOcGIyNHVZMjl0S0FBUAE?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN:en) [* Follow us on WhatsApp](https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaiosNqGE56fCGRIuX1Z) [* Share](# "Share on Facebook") [* Tweet](# "Tweet This Post") MUMBAI: Artificial intelligence is no longer just generating answers; it is generating serious money. Global AI software revenue is expected to cross $200 billion (€179.6 billion) in 2026, doubling its 2024 level as businesses accelerate investments in generative AI assistants, coding tools and increasingly autonomous systems, according to research firm Omdia. The forecast, outlined in Omdia’s Artificial Intelligence Software Market Forecasts, reflects a sharp acceleration in demand for both generative AI and agentic AI. The latest estimates represent the largest upward revision to the firm’s semi-annual market outlook since the Covid-19 pandemic, signalling that enterprise adoption is moving faster than previously anticipated. What makes the growth particularly unusual is that technology markets typically see annual expansion moderate as products mature and adoption spreads. AI software, however, is moving in the opposite direction, with businesses expanding deployments and technology providers racing to embed AI capabilities into their products. Generative AI revenue is now expected to grow by 139 per cent in 2026, significantly exceeding Omdia’s earlier projections. Enterprises are increasingly deploying AI assistants, coding tools and embedded AI capabilities across business applications, taking the technology beyond experimental projects and into everyday workflows. The expansion is being supported by growth across the wider AI value chain. Leading foundation model providers are recording year-on-year revenue growth of between three and ten times, while hyperscalers are reporting triple-digit expansion in their AI cloud segments. Enterprise software companies are adding another layer to the competition. Vendors are launching both AI-enhanced versions of existing products and entirely AI-native offerings, creating new revenue opportunities while intensifying competition for business customers. The shift suggests that AI is becoming a more integrated part of enterprise software rather than remaining a separate tool that employees access occasionally. From coding assistance to automated business processes, companies are increasingly looking to incorporate AI into the applications they already use. While generative AI currently commands greater attention and revenue, agentic AI is expanding even faster from a smaller base. Unlike conventional AI assistants that primarily respond to prompts or generate content, agentic systems are designed to take on tasks, make decisions within defined parameters and execute multiple steps with greater autonomy. AI Technical Insights # Gemma 4: Google’s Free Open Model, and Which Mac Can Run It By [Lenka Vojtechova](/author/lenka-vojtechova/)  ·  Updated November 12, 2026  ·  11 min read [Google](/tag/google/)[LLM](/tag/llm/)[Open-Source Model](/tag/open-source-model/)[Mac](/tag/mac/) ![Widescreen dark purple thumbnail reading ](/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/gemma-4-hero.webp) Gemma 4 is Google DeepMind’s family of free, open-weight AI models, announced on **2 April 2026** under the **Apache 2.0** licence. It now comes in **five sizes**, E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B A4B and 31B, and every one of them reads text and images and writes text. You download the weights once and run them on your own phone, laptop or server, with no subscription and no internet connection. The hard part is not getting Gemma 4. The hard part is picking the size your machine can actually hold. The names hide the memory bill. The “4B active” 26B model still needs room for all 26 billion parameters. This guide maps each Gemma 4 model to the Mac that runs it, using Google’s own memory figures. It then covers three ways to install it, its scores, how it stacks up against Qwen 3.6, and what it cannot do. ## The Key Takeaways > * **Five sizes, all free:** E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B A4B and 31B, under **Apache 2.0**, which allows commercial use. > * **Memory decides the model:** at 4-bit, Google lists **2.9GB** for E2B, **6.7GB** for the 12B and **17.5GB** for the 31B, before any context. > * **The Mac short version:** 8GB runs E2B, 16GB runs E4B or the 12B, the 26B A4B wants **24GB or more**, and the 31B is happiest at **32GB+**. > * **Strong for its size, not a frontier model:** the 31B scores **84.3%** on GPQA Diamond, but Alibaba’s own table puts Qwen3.6-27B ahead on coding, **77.2% vs 52.0%** on SWE-bench Verified. > * **Reads, does not draw:** Gemma 4 takes images (and audio on the small models) as input but only writes text, and its training data stops in **January 2025**. ## What Is Gemma 4? The Next Evolution Beyond Large Language Models ![James Dargan](https://theaiinsider.tech/wp-content/uploads/ultimatemember/526/profile_photo-80x80.png?1794389914)By [James Dargan](https://theaiinsider.tech/author/jamesdargan/) *·* *·* 5 min read ![](https://theaiinsider.tech/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-11-at-09.35.23-1024x572.png) For most of the generative AI era, progress has been measured in words. Large language models (LLMs) have been judged on how well they write, summarise, translate and reason in prose. Yet a growing share of the AI industry now argues that most real software workloads do not need a paragraph at all. They need an answer. That shift has given rise to AI decision models, systems built to choose rather than to talk. ### WHAT IS AN AI DECISION MODEL? An AI decision model is a system that returns a bounded, structured answer instead of free-form text. The application supplies the input, poses a question and defines the permitted answers in advance. The model then scores those options and returns a typed result, such as a selected label, a yes/no probability or a score on a defined scale, usually alongside a confidence value. As [jnaapti’s explainer on the category](https://jnaapti.com/articles/article/decision-models-history-and-evolution) illustrates, a support ticket about a missing payment might be scored against billing, shipping and returns, with the model selecting billing and returning a probability for each option, so the calling code never has to extract a label from generated prose. The same analysis notes that several of these models compute their scores in a single forward pass rather than generating output token by token, and that many accept new questions and answer options at call time. IT services group Coforgeframes the distinction in [enterprise terms](https://blog.coforge.com/blog/decision-intelligence-enterprise-ai-better-decisions-not-better-language): instead of asking a language model to write text and then inferring a decision from it, decision models are optimised to produce the decision itself, in the form of classifications, rankings, probabilities and confidence scores. ### WHY THE SHIFT FROM LANGUAGE TO DECISIONS The case for the category rests on a simple observation: most business processes exist to make judgments, not content. Coforge points to claims platforms deciding whether more evidence is required, underwriting systems choosing between approval, review and denial, and AI agents deciding whether to continue, retry, escalate or stop. Each is a choice among known options, and each affects cost, risk and compliance. DiploFoundation makes a similar argument from the infrastructure side. Its [analysis of decision-only AI](https://www.diplomacy.edu/blog/decision-only-ai-jev-governance/) observes that sensor anomalies in utilities and fault reports in public services are classification problems, where a label and a calibrated confidence score fit existing control logic far better than parsed prose. ### JEV AND THE RISE OF SYSTEM ONE MODELS Spam filters and intent classifiers have made bounded decisions for years, but 2026 changed the packaging. In September, TypeSafe AI [introduced Jev](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev), positioning it as a System One model, a nod to the distinction between fast intuitive judgment and slower deliberate reasoning [4]. AI Agents.content: × Search Pulse 2.0 # Plurai: $13 Million Seed Funding Led By Team8 To Advance AI Agent Simulation And Reliability Platform By Amit Chowdhry [![Pulse 2.0](https://pulse2.com/wp-content/themes/pulse2/images/logo-white.png)](https://pulse2.com "Pulse 2.0") Plurai: $13 Million Seed Funding Led By Team8 To Advance AI Agent Simulation And Reliability Platform [![Follow Pulse 2.0 on LinkedIn](https://pulse2.com/wp-content/themes/pulse2/images/inp2.png)](https://www.linkedin.com/company/pulse2news) Plurai, a New York-based developer of simulation infrastructure for artificial intelligence agents, announced $13 million in seed funding and the general availability of its platform. The company aims to help enterprises identify and correct AI agent failures before deployment while improving reliability, accuracy, and operating costs through simulation and specialized small language models (SLMs). The funding round was led by Team8, with participation from U&I, Velocity, and Mercer. More than 20 angel investors and industry executives also backed the company, including CyberArk founder Udi Mokady. Dr. Eyal Carmi, CTO of Microsoft 365 Copilot, has joined Plurai’s advisory board. Plurai’s platform addresses a growing challenge for enterprises adopting AI agents: ensuring that autonomous systems perform reliably in production environments. Although building agents has become increasingly accessible, testing their behavior across complex, unpredictable scenarios remains difficult and expensive. According to the company, its technology has helped design partners shorten agent development cycles from months to hours, reduce failures reaching real users by 82%, and lower the cost of operating reliable agents by 97%. Snowflake, Databricks, and other companies in this space have been working on different AI agents.  Chatbots are built to mostly respond to questions. Input and output. However, AI agents are built differently. They can actually get things done – without manual intervention or support from humans.  For example, AI agents can pull data from the enterprise system and they can work with different applications. They can (at least potentially) complete tasks without someone walking them through every step. That’s useful. But what happens when you have hundreds of these agents running across different departments? That makes it more complicated. How do you know what they’re all doing? To make matters even more complex, the AI agents won’t necessarily be running on the same platform. For example, the finance team might use one system. The marketing team or IT might use another. Some agents could be working with sensitive customer information. Others might have permission to update records or make changes to business applications. As senior vice president and head of ABAP Platform at SAP, she is responsible for ABAP and all matters related to ABAP platform. In this role, she is also the head of ABAP AI and thus globally responsible for the latest developments and innovations in this domain. ## **What is the Autonomous Enterprise? What part does ABAP platform play in it?** **Liénard:** At SAP Sapphire in 2026, we unveiled the [Autonomous Enterprise](https://www.sap.com/products/business-suite.html)—our vision for how we want to help large enterprises in the era of agentic AI. The fundamental shift we’re seeing is in the way people work with technology. Interfaces are no longer the focus: interaction is outcome-driven, not tool-driven. The user experience is being transformed. Instead of filling out forms in an application, you simply open a chat and ask: “Who was on vacation in the last 30 days, and when?” The answer comes back in real time. That’s the Autonomous Enterprise. The nature and purpose of ABAP platform is not changing. It is still the foundation on which business processes run—and it is now also the backbone on which agents operate. What *is* changing is the way users access applications. Agents now sit in front of those applications as an additional abstraction layer. If agents are expected to handle real business tasks—not demo scenarios, but actual financial postings, HR processes, or supply chain decisions—they need to run on a platform that is reliable, governed, and scalable. Get started with modern ABAP development [Find out how](https://www.sap.com/products/technology-platform/abap/environment.html) ## **Can you explain what ”outcome-driven” means?** Here’s an example. Instead of filling out a requisition form field by field, I open my chat and say, “I need 30 laptops for new hires by the end of October.” Agents check the catalog, review the budget, and create the requisition, without me having to navigate the process myself. As a user, I’m focused solely on the outcome, not on the route I need to take. When I enter a natural-language prompt, agents can autonomously pursue a variety of solution paths. What we’re seeing is a paradigm shift. The form-based environment we’re used to is giving way to the outcome-driven, agentic model. ## **What does designing a platform for agents involve?** It presents us with challenges on various levels. The first is reliability. Data and results must always be reliable, traceable, and reproducible—regardless of who triggered the agent or which path it took to obtain the data. This requires safety nets and very robust quality controls and tools. The next level is accountability and governance. Each agent must have a clearly defined authorization scope. What is it permitted to do? What is it *not* permitted to do? What data is it allowed to access? Agents need skills and workflows to follow. And there must also be an audit trail: what changes an agent made, who triggered the agent, and what exactly it was instructed to do. Well-defined interfaces are essential to ensure that agents operate strictly within their architectural boundaries, helping to prevent unauthorized data flows, close potential security gaps, and protect systems from compromise. AI Agents.titleZh: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers - CBS News
AI Agents.content: [Watch CBS News](/live/) # United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers By [Megan Cerullo Reporter, MoneyWatch](https://www.cbsnews.com/team/megan-cerullo/) Megan Cerullo is a New York-based reporter for CBS MoneyWatch covering small business, workplace, health care, consumer spending and personal finance topics. She regularly appears on CBS News 24/7 to discuss her reporting. [Read Full Bio](https://www.cbsnews.com/team/megan-cerullo/) [Megan Cerullo](https://www.cbsnews.com/team/megan-cerullo/) / MoneyWatch [Add CBS News on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=cbsnews.com) United Airlines said on Wednesday that it is banning artificial intelligence agents from making flight reservations on behalf of travelers, citing [security risks](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ai-agents-customer-bank-accounts-security/) and the possibility that such actions could violate federal rules. Many consumers are turning to AI agents such as [Meta's Muse](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/meta-ai-agent-muse-shopping/) and [OpenAI's dots](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/sam-altman-openai-dots-chatgpt-agents-safety/) to complete tasks ranging from researching products and tracking down deals to making purchases. To make an airline booking, an AI agent requires access to a customer's personal information, including credentials like payment information. United has a problem with that, saying that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." The carrier also said that using an AI agent to, for example, check in for a flight could violate federal regulations, including rules requiring travelers to verify in person that their luggage does not contain banned substances. "As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants," said the airline, which is updating its booking and ticketing policies to reflect the new rule. United's new policy suggests the company wants to retain control over the customer booking process, said Henry Harteveldt, an aviation analyst at Atmosphere Research Group. "United is saying they don't want to add yet another, and potentially even more powerful, intermediary than they already face in terms of Google search, price-comparison metasearch sites and online travel agencies," he told CBS News. "Flight searches cost airlines money, and undoubtedly United wants to avoid the expense associated with the surge of AI bot flight searches." Other airlines are taking a different tack to the emergence of AI agents. For example, Southwest has made its flight inventory viewable to ChatGPT users, who can access the airline's website through the AI app. United fares will continue to be bookable through flight aggregators such as Kayak, Hopper and Google Flights, Harteveldt said, adding that "consumers shouldn't find it any more difficult to find good fares on the airline." "But by blocking the AI bots, United won't make it any easier to find its fares, either," he said. Edited by [Alain Sherter](https://www.cbsnews.com/team/alain-sherter/) [Kris Van Cleave](https://www.cbsnews.com/team/kris-van-cleave/) contributed to this report. LLMs.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Best Local LLM for Coding: $0 Weights vs $2 API [2026] ![Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/tvance.webp) [Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/author/tvance/) Updated Nov 12, 2026 · 26 min read The best local LLM for coding in mid-November 2026 depends less on a leaderboard score than on three constraints: how much memory your machine has, what license the weights carry, and whether you can verify the files you download. Google’s [Gemma 4 family, released under Apache 2.0 with commercial use allowed](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemma-4/), OpenAI’s gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b, and Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3.1 Pro all compete for the same developer attention, yet they sit at very different points on the hardware ladder. Choosing among them is harder than the headlines suggest. Parameter counts run from small on-device variants to a model that Moonshot describes at the 3-trillion level, and “open” means something different in each license file. Readers who want the licensing side in isolation can start with our [open-weight license comparison](https://shattered.io/open-weight-models-license-comparison-6-families-16gb-2026/). The narrower question is which of these models should actually sit behind your editor, terminal agent or CI job. The short answer, with the evidence below. For a single developer with a 16 GB-class machine, gpt-oss-20b is the safest starting point because OpenAI ships it under Apache 2.0 and documents a small memory footprint. For a team with an 80 GB-class workstation, gpt-oss-120b is the next step up. Gemma 4 is the pick when you want the cleanest license and a size for every machine. Kimi K3.1 Pro is a server-class model, not a laptop model. DeepSeek, Qwen and Llama stay on the watch list because the evidence we could verify today does not support ranking them for local use. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Run a Coding Model on Your Own Hardware in November 2026 Three reasons keep pulling developers toward local inference: code privacy, cost predictability and independence from someone else’s deprecation calendar. The third reason got a live demonstration this week. On November 10, 2026, DigitalOcean published a release note that [pulled several open models from its serverless inference product](https://docs.digitalocean.com/notes/2026/inference-deprecate-oss-models-nov-2026/). The notice names Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct, and a research summary of the same notice reports that Gemma 4, Qwen 3.5 397B A17B and DeepSeek V4 Flash left serverless inference too, with DigitalOcean pointing users toward DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Gemma 4 stayed available on dedicated inference. Nothing was discontinued by its maker. A hosting decision simply removed a cheap endpoint, and every team that had wired a pipeline to it had to migrate. Weights on your own disk do not get deprecated that way. If you pin a model file and a runtime version, the behavior of your coding assistant stays the same next month, which matters when your test suite or your review bot depends on consistent output. That stability is the strongest practical argument for local, stronger than raw price. ### What the industry data says about open models Adoption data points the same direction, though unevenly. IDC’s 2025 FutureScape predictions for Asia-Pacific (excluding Japan) state: “By 2026, 60% of Asia-Pacific organizations are predicted to build applications using open-source AI foundation models.” The source is IDC’s developer and DevOps predictions document, and the figure is a forecast, not a measured result. AI Technical Insights # Gemma 4: Google’s Free Open Model, and Which Mac Can Run It By [Lenka Vojtechova](/author/lenka-vojtechova/)  ·  Updated November 12, 2026  ·  11 min read [Google](/tag/google/)[LLM](/tag/llm/)[Open-Source Model](/tag/open-source-model/)[Mac](/tag/mac/) ![Widescreen dark purple thumbnail reading ](/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/gemma-4-hero.webp) Gemma 4 is Google DeepMind’s family of free, open-weight AI models, announced on **2 April 2026** under the **Apache 2.0** licence. It now comes in **five sizes**, E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B A4B and 31B, and every one of them reads text and images and writes text. You download the weights once and run them on your own phone, laptop or server, with no subscription and no internet connection. The hard part is not getting Gemma 4. The hard part is picking the size your machine can actually hold. The names hide the memory bill. The “4B active” 26B model still needs room for all 26 billion parameters. This guide maps each Gemma 4 model to the Mac that runs it, using Google’s own memory figures. It then covers three ways to install it, its scores, how it stacks up against Qwen 3.6, and what it cannot do. ## The Key Takeaways > * **Five sizes, all free:** E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B A4B and 31B, under **Apache 2.0**, which allows commercial use. > * **Memory decides the model:** at 4-bit, Google lists **2.9GB** for E2B, **6.7GB** for the 12B and **17.5GB** for the 31B, before any context. > * **The Mac short version:** 8GB runs E2B, 16GB runs E4B or the 12B, the 26B A4B wants **24GB or more**, and the 31B is happiest at **32GB+**. > * **Strong for its size, not a frontier model:** the 31B scores **84.3%** on GPQA Diamond, but Alibaba’s own table puts Qwen3.6-27B ahead on coding, **77.2% vs 52.0%** on SWE-bench Verified. > * **Reads, does not draw:** Gemma 4 takes images (and audio on the small models) as input but only writes text, and its training data stops in **January 2025**. ## What Is Gemma 4? The Next Evolution Beyond Large Language Models ![James Dargan](https://theaiinsider.tech/wp-content/uploads/ultimatemember/526/profile_photo-80x80.png?1794389914)By [James Dargan](https://theaiinsider.tech/author/jamesdargan/) *·* *·* 5 min read ![](https://theaiinsider.tech/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-11-at-09.35.23-1024x572.png) For most of the generative AI era, progress has been measured in words. Large language models (LLMs) have been judged on how well they write, summarise, translate and reason in prose. Yet a growing share of the AI industry now argues that most real software workloads do not need a paragraph at all. They need an answer. That shift has given rise to AI decision models, systems built to choose rather than to talk. ### WHAT IS AN AI DECISION MODEL? An AI decision model is a system that returns a bounded, structured answer instead of free-form text. The application supplies the input, poses a question and defines the permitted answers in advance. The model then scores those options and returns a typed result, such as a selected label, a yes/no probability or a score on a defined scale, usually alongside a confidence value. As [jnaapti’s explainer on the category](https://jnaapti.com/articles/article/decision-models-history-and-evolution) illustrates, a support ticket about a missing payment might be scored against billing, shipping and returns, with the model selecting billing and returning a probability for each option, so the calling code never has to extract a label from generated prose. The same analysis notes that several of these models compute their scores in a single forward pass rather than generating output token by token, and that many accept new questions and answer options at call time. IT services group Coforgeframes the distinction in [enterprise terms](https://blog.coforge.com/blog/decision-intelligence-enterprise-ai-better-decisions-not-better-language): instead of asking a language model to write text and then inferring a decision from it, decision models are optimised to produce the decision itself, in the form of classifications, rankings, probabilities and confidence scores. ### WHY THE SHIFT FROM LANGUAGE TO DECISIONS The case for the category rests on a simple observation: most business processes exist to make judgments, not content. Coforge points to claims platforms deciding whether more evidence is required, underwriting systems choosing between approval, review and denial, and AI agents deciding whether to continue, retry, escalate or stop. Each is a choice among known options, and each affects cost, risk and compliance. DiploFoundation makes a similar argument from the infrastructure side. Its [analysis of decision-only AI](https://www.diplomacy.edu/blog/decision-only-ai-jev-governance/) observes that sensor anomalies in utilities and fault reports in public services are classification problems, where a label and a calibrated confidence score fit existing control logic far better than parsed prose. ### JEV AND THE RISE OF SYSTEM ONE MODELS Spam filters and intent classifiers have made bounded decisions for years, but 2026 changed the packaging. In September, TypeSafe AI [introduced Jev](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev), positioning it as a System One model, a nod to the distinction between fast intuitive judgment and slower deliberate reasoning [4]. Open Source AI.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Best Local LLM for Coding: $0 Weights vs $2 API [2026] ![Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/tvance.webp) [Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/author/tvance/) Updated Nov 12, 2026 · 26 min read The best local LLM for coding in mid-November 2026 depends less on a leaderboard score than on three constraints: how much memory your machine has, what license the weights carry, and whether you can verify the files you download. Google’s [Gemma 4 family, released under Apache 2.0 with commercial use allowed](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemma-4/), OpenAI’s gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b, and Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3.1 Pro all compete for the same developer attention, yet they sit at very different points on the hardware ladder. Choosing among them is harder than the headlines suggest. Parameter counts run from small on-device variants to a model that Moonshot describes at the 3-trillion level, and “open” means something different in each license file. Readers who want the licensing side in isolation can start with our [open-weight license comparison](https://shattered.io/open-weight-models-license-comparison-6-families-16gb-2026/). The narrower question is which of these models should actually sit behind your editor, terminal agent or CI job. The short answer, with the evidence below. For a single developer with a 16 GB-class machine, gpt-oss-20b is the safest starting point because OpenAI ships it under Apache 2.0 and documents a small memory footprint. For a team with an 80 GB-class workstation, gpt-oss-120b is the next step up. Gemma 4 is the pick when you want the cleanest license and a size for every machine. Kimi K3.1 Pro is a server-class model, not a laptop model. DeepSeek, Qwen and Llama stay on the watch list because the evidence we could verify today does not support ranking them for local use. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Run a Coding Model on Your Own Hardware in November 2026 Three reasons keep pulling developers toward local inference: code privacy, cost predictability and independence from someone else’s deprecation calendar. The third reason got a live demonstration this week. On November 10, 2026, DigitalOcean published a release note that [pulled several open models from its serverless inference product](https://docs.digitalocean.com/notes/2026/inference-deprecate-oss-models-nov-2026/). Open Source AI.content: [![TIER IV](https://tier4.co.jp/hubfs/files/images/logo.svg)](/?hsLang=en) November 11, 2026 Press release # TIER IV unveils end-to-end autonomous driving adaptable to map information and sensor configurations ## Multiple open-source AI models are available with Autoware Tokyo, November 11, 2026 – [TIER IV](/en/?hsLang=en), the pioneering force behind Autoware, open-source software for autonomous driving, today announced the development and open-source release of multiple end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving AI models that support different system requirements, including map information and sensor configurations. The models offer flexible options ranging from camera-only configurations to those incorporating LiDAR, radar and high-definition (HD) maps, enabling developers to select AI models suited to their performance requirements. Through Autoware, TIER IV provides a development environment for optimizing these models and integrating them into vehicle systems, helping automakers and technology partners develop and deploy their own autonomous driving stack. ### Overview of the Autoware 2.0 Architecture TIER IV is leading the [development of Autoware 2.0](/en/updates/press-release/20261102-tieriv-spearheads-autoware2.0-initiatives?hsLang=en), the next-generation architecture of Autoware. Autoware 2.0 is a scalable and adaptable architecture that flexibly combines AI models with conventional rule-based technologies. By supporting different AI models and sensor configurations, it enables autonomous driving systems to be built for a range of applications and system requirements. The E2E autonomous driving AI models announced today are concrete technological outcomes designed to leverage this architecture. ### NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge As part of its [collaboration with NVIDIA](/en/updates/press-release/20260319?hsLang=en) announced in March 2026 , TIER IV has been evaluating the performance of NVIDIA Alpamayo, a vision-language-action (VLA) foundation model, and integrating it with Autoware. It adopts a Fast–Slow architecture combining a Reactive Model for real-time driving decisions, a World Model for predicting future changes in the surrounding environment, and a Reasoning Model that supports driving decisions. It can accommodate configurations ranging from cameras alone to those incorporating LiDAR and radar sensor data. With 79.9 million parameters, it is lighter than Alpamayo 2 Edge. The Reactive Model has been released, while development of the World Model and Reasoning Model continues, alongside consideration of commercialization for robotaxi applications. Integration of the Reactive Model with Autoware has been achieved. * GitHub (source code): <https://github.com/autowarefoundation/auto_e2e> * Hugging Face (AI model): <https://huggingface.co/AutowareFoundation/auto_e2e> ### METEOR Developed independently by TIER IV, [METEOR](/en/updates/technology/20260908-reference-e2e-model?hsLang=en) is a lightweight, multitask E2E autonomous driving AI model primarily intended for privately owned passenger vehicles...

Sand3D is a Python library for describing 3D objects as programs that language models can write and people can inspect. Its structured approach lets users build models from named parts, then export them for design and simulation workflows. ![The Sandflow-ai/sand3d repository page on GitHub](https://news.lavx.hu/api/media/file/sandflow-ai-sand3d-github-2026-11-11.png) *Screenshot: GitHub* ## What it is Sand3D represents a 3D object as a Python program that describes how someone builds it. The program can define profiles, turn them into solids, edit those solids, place parts in relation to one another and assemble the result. That structure gives a language model a compact way to describe geometry while leaving a person with code they can read and change. The project targets users who want generated 3D objects to carry their construction history in an inspectable form. The library treats an object as a set of named parts rather than an opaque mesh. A part can include its shape, position and relationship to neighboring parts, so a user can refer to edges and faces by name instead of calculating coordinates by hand. Sand3D also aims for repeatable output: the README says the same program produces the same mesh. This makes a model's source code useful for both inspecting its design and making later edits. ## How it works A Sand3D program combines geometry operations through a Python interface. A user can sketch a profile, extrude or revolve it into a solid, then apply changes such as holes, cuts, fillets or chamfers. Placement tools let the program position parts in local frames or arrange them in patterns. The code records those operations as named steps, giving the final object a readable structure that a person or language model can revise without rebuilding the whole shape from scratch. For objects with moving parts, a program can group components and define joints between them. A joint can describe a hinge, a sliding connection or continuous rotation, while a pose can set the assembly's position. The README uses a washing machine to show how a door, drum, drawer and dial can form one assembly with separate movement rules. That approach supports models whose parts need to move as well as objects that stay fixed. ## Key features Sand3D groups its operations around profiles, solids, paths, edits, placement, articulation, assemblies, parts and materials. Users can start from basic shapes such as rectangles, circles and boxes, or create profiles from curves and text. Cinecode gives filmmakers a way to make videos through an AI coding agent that writes scripts, builds images in code and designs sound. The creator chooses the film’s direction and reviews drafts before the agent produces an MP4. ![The sarpstar/cinecode repository page on GitHub](https://news.lavx.hu/api/media/file/sarpstar-cinecode-github-2026-11-11.png) *Screenshot: GitHub* ## What it is Cinecode is a filmmaking kit for people who want to turn an idea into a finished video with help from an AI coding agent. The creator supplies the concept and taste; the agent develops a script, renders frames through code, designs audio and produces an MP4. The project supports short films, longer video essays and documentaries, advertisements, explainers and music videos. Its process gives the creator choices about a film’s style and sound as the agent builds it. The kit treats filmmaking as a sequence of creative decisions and review points. A creator can ask for a story built around an unexpected real-world reference, such as an artifact, animal, invention or place. The kit also checks a proposed idea against the creator’s past films to reduce repeated suggestions. Before the render grows into a full film, the creator picks a visual approach and reviews sample scenes. The workflow suits people who want an AI agent to handle production tasks while they retain direction over the result. ## How it works The agent starts by asking about the idea, format, duration, visual style, voice and music. It then presents a plan with timed beats and a director’s board that the creator can edit. The creator reviews sample frames before the agent renders the rest. During a draft, the kit checks motion, sound level, text legibility and repetition; a separate viewer agent also reviews the cut. The creator’s notes guide revisions to the parts they address, and the final stage produces a full-size video with mastered sound and a credits file. Cinecode offers Quick mode for a more direct production path and Film mode for projects with research or several scenes. Quick mode places scenes, sound and text in a self-contained film file, then renders a draft for review. Film mode moves through a roadmap, script, style frame, animatic and render, with creator approval at selected stages. The creator can move a project from Quick mode into Film mode, carrying its beats into a broader plan. The agent chooses a mode to fit the project’s scope. ## Key features The visual tools cover several production styles, from cinematic scenes to animation, collage, clay-like imagery and graphic design. Open Source AI.content: # [opensource.google.com](https://opensource.google.com/ "Google Open Source") [Menu](/#Navigation "Nav Toggle Open") ## [Google Open Source Blog](/ "Google Open Source Blog") The latest news from Google on open source releases, major projects, events, and outreach programs for early career developers. ### Scaling AI agents with open standards: Kurtis Van Gent on MCP and Agent Skills joining the AAIF #### Wednesday, November 11, 2026 ![MCP Toolbox for Databases architecture diagram showing database engines connected via MCP servers to developer tools and AI clients](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhLCywvRZwLvoKa7EobHGksI6daxbSsoZQWZp5fW7_9JkLfQLBmGnt75sV-uZV8S-7Anm7ofOlAjHJcTi5XlYBlk4V2Ujgg-ptSyE7hnVLNN5Fx2KU5uLOL_sYCn2sCFI9YWONOtb5pEYM1-VvzFzsQo5oDdgBV59XvjQIQ9ssRamjNlx0rljgHrZzH90A/s1600/image.png) by Kurtis Van Gent, Google Cloud, and Daryl Ducharme, Google Open Source Programs Office Building production AI agents requires more than a capable reasoning model. Agents need a reliable way to connect to external systems and data, and they need procedural domain knowledge so they know how to use those tools safely without exhausting their context window. Over the past year, open source communities have rallied around two complementary open standards to solve these challenges: the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) for connecting agents to live tools, and [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/) for loading procedural instructions and scripts on demand. Following Anthropic's donation of the Agent Skills specification to the Linux Foundation's [Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)](https://aaif.io/) alongside MCP, engineers from Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, and the wider ecosystem are now co-maintaining the standard under vendor-neutral governance. To explore how open standards prevent ecosystem fragmentation, and why the best solutions don't always have to be homegrown, we sat down with Kurtis Van Gent, co-creator of the open source [MCP Toolbox for Databases](https://github.com/googleapis/genai-toolbox) and a core maintainer on both MCP and Agent Skills. ## From the N-by-M database problem to open source collaboration **Daryl Ducharme:** How did your work on AI ecosystems for Google Cloud Databases and co-creating the open source MCP Toolbox for Databases lead to your role as a core maintainer on both the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent Skills? **Kurtis Van Gent:** When I started my current role around three years ago, it was early in the generative AI cycle. My mission was to make it easy for developers to use cloud databases for their AI applications. As a strong proponent of developer experience, I loved that charter. As model reasoning improved, context and data were clearly the keys to making effective use of it, and there's no better place to store data than a database. At the time, most database conversations focused on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) using vector search. However, our team believed that agents and tools held the most interesting potential for large language models (LLMs) going forward. We immediately hit two scaling challenges: Google Cloud supports more than 15 different databases across its portfolio, and new open source agent frameworks (starting with LangChain and LlamaIndex) were emerging every week. That created a classic N-by-M integration problem between many clients and many data hosts. To solve it, we started GenAI Toolbox for Databases (now [MCP Toolbox for Databases](https://github.com/googleapis/genai-toolbox)) as an open source framework for building and serving tools. We built our own server, clients, and protocol to standardize how agents look up and invoke database tools. Back then, agent terminology wasn't common vernacular yet, so every talk I gave had to start with three to five slides explaining what agents and tools actually were. When Anthropic announced MCP, it was exciting validation that the broader ecosystem was arriving ...

Infra & Chips.content: [Skip to Main Content](#aws-page-content-main) AWS Blogs * [Home](/blogs/) * Blogs * Editions ## [Artificial Intelligence](/blogs/machine-learning/) # The attendee’s guide to the AWS re:Invent 2026 AI/ML track From November 30th to December 4th, Amazon Web Services (AWS) will hold its annual premier learning event: [re:Invent](/events/reinvent/). At this event, attendees will become stronger and more proficient in various areas of AWS technology through a variety of experiences: keynotes given by AWS leaders, interactive working sessions led by AWS experts, and [fun, immersive activities such as live entertainment and games at re:Play](/events/reinvent/experiences/uniquely-reinvent/). There are over [2,000 learning sessions](https://registration.awsevents.com/flow/awsevents/reinvent2026/eventcatalog/page/eventcatalog?search=) that focus on specific topics at various skill levels, and the AI/ML (AIM) track has more than [140 unique sessions](https://registration.awsevents.com/flow/awsevents/reinvent2026/eventcatalog/page/eventcatalog?search=AIM) for you to choose from. We’re here to help you identify the sessions that best fit your needs. Even if you can’t join in person, you can catch up with many of the sessions on demand and even watch the keynotes live. ## The basics: Session types If you can join us, then remember that we offer several types of sessions that can help maximize your learning in a variety of AWS topics. re:Invent attendees can choose to attend breakouts, chalk talks, builder sessions, workshops, and code talks. The breakout sessions are recorded and uploaded a few days after to the [AWS Events YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@AWSEventsChannel), while the rest are live non-recorded interactive sessions. Here are the details for each session type: * **Breakout sessions:** Attendees are in a lecture-style 60-minute informative session presented by AWS experts, customers, and partners. * **Chalk-talk sessions:** Attendees interact with presenters, asking questions, and using a whiteboard in session. * **Builder sessions:** Attendees participate in a one-hour session and build something. * **Workshop sessions:** Attendees join a two-hour interactive session where you work in a small team to solve a real problem using AWS services. * **Code talk sessions:** Attendees participate in engaging code-focused sessions where an expert leads a live coding session. * **Lightning talk sessions:** Attendees watch a 20-minute demo dedicated to either a specific service or customer story (located in the Venetian Expo Hall or Wynn/Encore Upper Convention Promenade). With so many sessions to pick from, it helps to know how the pieces fit together. Here is how AWS thinks about its AI offerings, so you can decide where to begin and where to focus. ## The AWS AI stack overview and tie-in to re:Invent sessions AWS offers a comprehensive AI portfolio in the cloud. It covers everything from the physical infrastructure and AI chips that power AI workloads up through ready-to-use agentic solutions that teams can adopt today. Understanding how these services work together helps you navigate re:Invent and focus on the sessions most relevant to what you’re building. Infra & Chips.content: In this article The swirl of sex-and-spying allegations around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is raising a worrying question: Could trouble at the chipmaker spread through the tightly connected financial network Nvidia has built to support the artificial intelligence boom? Serious problems with Nvidia could do far-reaching economic and financial damage. The company has made hundreds of billions of dollars in financial commitments to other firms to help the industry grow, earning it the nickname the "central bank of AI." The Federal Reserve and other financial institutions are closely watching the AI buildout to monitor for the possibility that an unexpected event could destabilize the global financial system. Even back in July Fed officials were discussing the possibility of of a "broad-based repricing of assets" in the event of problems in the AI sector. A rerun of the 2007-2008 financial crisis isn't likely, according to analysts and current and former financial officials. Nvidia isn't "too big to fail in a bank sense at all," said Sheila Bair, a former government regulator who ran the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. Unlike a troubled bank, Nvidia isn't vulnerable to a sudden loss of confidence and would still produce a product customers want to buy even if something went wrong. And its massive equity gives it a cushion. But regulators need to watch carefully for exposure by the banks and the wider financial system to Nvidia and other firms like it, Bair said. "Nvidia going down would be a pretty seismic event," she said. Investors still have high hopes for Nvidia, which reports earnings on Tuesday. Analysts expect its revenue to more than double in the current fiscal year, and then to roughly double again over the following two years, according to LSEG data. But with Huang under scrutiny by the FBI, Congress, and Nvidia's board over his relationship with a woman who The New York Times reported was suspected of spying for China, analysts see a wide range of outcomes as suddenly possible, including the potential removal of Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993. The company didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Nvidia's board has expressed confidence in its CEO. Nvidia's stock fell 30% from its Oct. 6 peak through Tuesday's close, amid a broader reassessment of the AI trade prompted by Democrats' surprising victory in the Nov. 3 midterms. Its stock recovered Wednesday, rising more than 4% as of midday. Still, people who closely track the financial flows underlying AI say that even sharper losses by Nvidia likely wouldn't trigger the kind of systemic problems that regulators guard against. And yet the risks flowing from AI are keeping some finance officials up at night. They are watching for the possibility that many of the factors that have helped the AI boom could reverse simultaneously. If the value of Nvidia's GPU chips fell, for instance, it could prompt investors to ask whether companies that borrowed money to buy them would be able to pay off their debts. In that case, the financial assistance big tech firms have extended to others in the industry could suddenly become drags on their growth. Tech companies would have credit problems at the same time that their equity is falling. Problems among giant tech firms wouldn't stay contained to tech investors' portfolios, but could cause problems across the economy. "I think that's a real concern because both the economy and financial markets are standing on the same leg, which means a drawdown could have reinforcing effects between the two," said Jason Wu, an assistant director at the International Monetary Fund who oversees the Global Markets Analysis unit. Wu was the lead author of a chapter of the IMF's Global Financial Stability report published in October that warned about the potential for growing leverage among AI firms and investors to trigger broader problems. The decline followed allegations concerning Huang’s relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities are said to have identified as a Chinese intelligence asset. For now, the allegation has not been independently verified. China’s foreign ministry has rejected the espionage claims as groundless. ### Trump confirms FBI scrutiny as Nvidia begins its own investigation Trump said on Monday that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the matter. “I know the FBI is looking into it,” Trump said, adding that he believed Huang would “be in good shape.” The president said Huang had told him that he did not know the woman was allegedly connected to Chinese intelligence. A committee of independent directors, supported by outside legal counsel, will supervise the investigation. The company said it had no reason to believe that either American national security or Nvidia’s confidential information had been compromised. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate,” Nvidia said in its official statement⁠. The inquiry does not establish wrongdoing by Huang, and there has been no official finding that Nvidia technology or sensitive information was transferred through the relationship. ### New chip-shipment allegations deepen Nvidia’s market losses The latest share-price decline followed a report that the relationship helped facilitate at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia-chip shipments to Chinese companies. The report alleged that a network of companies in China and Singapore helped obtain and route approximately 240,000 Nvidia H100, H200 and A100 processors into China. Some of those chip models are subject to American export restrictions intended to limit China’s access to advanced computing technology.
